title: AWS IAM Role Policy Attachment

compliance.assurance_rationale: Saved search evidence for AU-2 when alert outputs are archived.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay or inject sample `aws:cloudtrail` events matching `(eventName="AttachRolePolicy" OR eventName="PutRolePolicy" OR eventName="DetachRolePolicy" OR eventName="DeleteRolePolicy")` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.1.85 search returns >=1 row and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:cloudtrail` traffic without `(eventName="AttachRolePolicy" OR eventName="PutRolePolicy" OR eventName="DetachRolePolicy" OR eventName="DeleteRolePolicy")` markers. Confirm the search returns zero rows and alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudtrail` collected via Splunk Add-on for AWS (`Splunk_TA_aws`, Splunkbase 1876); validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure Splunk Add-on for AWS (`Splunk_TA_aws`, Splunkbase 1876) with the modular input for `aws:cloudtrail`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable organization-wide CloudTrail with management and data events for iam. Configure `Splunk_TA_aws` CloudTrail S3 or CloudWatch Logs input into `index=aws`. Save as a real-time alert on matching `AttachRolePolicy` events; tune exclusions via saved lookup for break-glass roles.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" (eventName="AttachRolePolicy" OR eventName="PutRolePolicy" OR eventName="DetachRolePolicy" OR eventName="DeleteRolePolicy")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.85_aws_iam_role_policy_atta_85"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudtrail` in `index=aws` to detect aws iam role policy attachment. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS CloudTrail console Event history for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_85_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Events list (critical alert), Timeline by eventName, Table of actor and resource..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Splunk Add-on for AWS (`Splunk_TA_aws`, Splunkbase 1876) and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of aws iam role policy attachment so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
